title: 心理学 Day 6：自我同情 — 给自己的话，能换成给朋友的吗？
title_en: Psychology Day 6: Self-Compassion — Could You Say That to a Friend?

questions.question: 研究显示，得到自我同情提示的人失败后更愿意重做任务、投入更久。按文章的解释，自我同情提升动机的机制是什么？
options: 拿掉羞耻之后，人才敢正视自己的错误，学习也才有可能发生
它带来愉快的情绪奖励，用好心情抵消了失败带来的疲惫感
它降低了对自己的标准，目标变得容易达成，于是更愿意尝试
它像高自尊一样让人相信自己比别人强，因而更有信心再赢一次
questions.explanation: 文章的链条是：羞耻导致回避、回避阻断学习；同情带来安全感，能正视错误才会学习。文章明确说自我同情不降低标准，也把它与依赖比较、要求赢的自尊区分开。
questions.question_en: Studies found that people prompted toward self-compassion were more willing to retry a failed task and kept at it longer. By the article's account, how does self-compassion raise motivation?
options_en: Removing shame lets people face their mistakes squarely, which is what makes learning possible
It delivers a pleasant emotional reward, and the good mood offsets the fatigue that failure brings
It lowers the standards people hold themselves to, so goals feel easier and they try more readily
Like high self-esteem, it makes people believe they outperform others, boosting confidence to win again
questions.explanation_en: The article's chain: shame breeds avoidance, avoidance blocks learning; compassion brings safety, and facing errors is what lets learning happen. It states plainly that self-compassion doesn't lower standards, and it distinguishes it from self-esteem, which depends on comparison and needs to win.

questions.question: 孩子沮丧地说「只有我考砸了」。按文章对共通人性的理解，哪种回应最贴切？
options: 「一次考试而已，真没什么大不了，别再为这件事难过了。」
「下次复习再认真一点，你肯定就能考出好成绩来。」
「每个人都会有搞砸的感觉，这就是人在学习的样子。」
「班上肯定有人考得比你还差，你根本不是最差的那个。」
questions.explanation: 文章特别提醒不要说「别人也有考差的」，那是比较；共通人性是承认痛苦的强度，同时把它放回人类共有的处境，「AND 不是 BUT」。说没什么大不了，则是在淡化痛苦。
questions.question_en: A child says dejectedly, “I'm the only one who flunked.” Based on the article's idea of common humanity, which response fits best?
options_en: “It's just one test, honestly no big deal, so stop being upset about it.”
“Just study a bit harder next time and you'll definitely get a good score.”
“Everyone has that feeling of messing up—it's part of how people learn.”
“I'm sure someone in your class did worse—you're definitely not the worst.”
questions.explanation_en: The article specifically warns against “others did badly too,” which is comparison. Common humanity acknowledges how much it hurts while placing it within a shared human experience—“and,” not “but.” Calling it no big deal is minimizing.

questions.question: 一位长期照顾家人、习惯忍让的人已经耗竭，身边人还常常得寸进尺。按文章的 tender/fierce 框架，此时更该加强的是什么？
options: 凶猛的自我同情：划清边界、说不，为被苛待的自己挺身而出
更严格地反省自己哪里做得不够，用高标准逼自己走出低落状态
先把照顾的事做得无可挑剔，等压力小了再练习自我同情
柔软的自我同情：更多地安慰和接纳自己，继续练习包容身边的人
questions.explanation: 文章指出照顾者型往往 tender 多、fierce 缺，结果是耗竭和被剥削；对长期 tender 偏多的人，fierce 才是疗愈入口，不是更多忍耐。「先把事做好再来自我同情」被文章明确称为把顺序弄倒了。
questions.question_en: Someone who has long cared for family and habitually gives way is now burned out, and people around them keep taking more. Under the article's tender/fierce framework, what should they build up?
options_en: Fierce self-compassion: drawing boundaries, saying no, standing up for the self that has been mistreated
Scrutinize more strictly where they fall short, using high standards to push out of the slump
Make their caregiving flawless first, and start practicing self-compassion once the pressure eases
Tender self-compassion: more comforting and accepting of themselves, while continuing to accommodate others
questions.explanation_en: The article notes that caretaker types tend to have plenty of tender and too little fierce, ending in exhaustion and exploitation; for them, fierce self-compassion—not more endurance—is the way in. “Do the work first, self-compassion later” is something the article explicitly calls backwards.
